videos.title: How to Protect Water for 40M People on the Colorado River | WSJ Pro Perfected
videos.description:
About 40 million people rely on the Colorado River. But an extended drought and a century-old legal framework have pushed the system to a breaking point. Now, a federal plan threatening deep cuts has ignited a fierce political and legal war across the Southwest.

WSJ spoke with Arizona State University water law professor Rhett Larson, who broke down where the government’s framework falls short, why easy fixes won't solve the issue, and what structural overhauls are needed to protect a crucial regional economy.

videos.title: Paschal Donohoe and Elisabeth Svantesson on Jobs, Private Capital and Global Cooperation
videos.description:
In conversation with Paschal, the Chair of the Development Committee – Sweden’s Minister for Finance, Elisabeth Svantesson – reflects on the World Bank Group’s evolving role in an increasingly complex world. She discusses why strong institutions, meaningful jobs, private capital, and open dialogue among governments are essential to improving lives, especially for young people. Drawing on her experience as chair, Minister Svantesson shares how stronger relationships and candid conversations can build consensus and turn “people, policy, and process” into lasting progress.

videos.title: Why This Deep Red State Is a Battleground for the GOP’s Future | WSJ
videos.description:
Idaho, deeply Republican and mostly rural, is about the furthest you could get from a battleground state. So it is no surprise it is often overlooked in the national media during midterm elections.

But under the surface there is a groundswell of tensions between traditional Republicans, the MAGA loyalists and newer hardline-right politicians tussling for power and influence in Idaho. This Mountain West state has become a key bellwether for the fight over what a post-Trump Republican Party could become at the national level, as well as a test lab for some of the nation’s most controversial conservative legislation.

WSJ’s Robbie Gramer returns to his home state of Idaho to explore what the tensions between Idaho’s traditional Republicans and a newer, hard-line political right could mean for the Republican party’s national identity ahead of the midterms.

Chapters:
0:00 Idaho’s midterm elections
1:24 The battle for the soul of the Republican Party
3:38 Bills on social issues and the Idaho Freedom Foundation
6:43 Immigration issues

videos.description:
ZVERNEC, ALBANIA – On the doorstep of a Jared Kushner-linked development site, a group of determined villagers set out in late May to protest barbed-wire fencing preventing their access to a coastal peninsula. 

A video of the scene captured security guards punching one resident in the throat and dragging him along the beach by his arms. The incident sparked outrage and inspired a nationwide protest movement dubbed the “Flamingo Revolution,” with demonstrators calling for an end to the plans for a luxury resort and for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama. 

WSJ analyzes Albanian court documents, travels to the development areas, and speaks to the villagers at the heart of disputes over land ownership.

videos.title: Why It's So Expensive To Run An Auto Repair Shop
videos.description:

Shops are spending more on software access and safety calibration equipment. While the number of auto repair shops has grown, some who work in the business say it is getting harder to keep up, especially for smaller ones.

videos.title: What Democrats Actually Think of the Party, the DSA and Midterms | WSJ
videos.description:
Democrats are on track to make gains in the November midterm elections, but they’re benefiting from President Trump’s unpopularity—not their own party’s image. In fact, Democrats have received some of their lowest approval ratings ever since Trump took office last year. 

Democratic voters are divided over what they believe their party should stand for and who is best equipped to beat Republicans. The party’s far-left flank has been ascendent with members of the Democratic Socialists of America and other progressives toppling longtime incumbents in some party primaries. For the first time ever, several highly competitive Senate and House seats will have far-left candidates as the Democratic nominees—a test of progressive power in competitive races. 

We asked a group of Democratic voters from across the country to join us to talk about the party at this moment. Watch the video to learn more. 

In the coming weeks we will have a video discussion with young men who voted for Trump in 2024. A year ago we spoke to a group of them to get their read on Trump’s first six months in office. We brought them back together to see how they feel about the administration now.

videos.title: How Arc’teryx Became a $2B+ Luxury Brand Without Intending To | WSJ The Economics Of
videos.description:
A $900 Arc’teryx Alpha SV jacket has more than 150 component parts from more than 35 suppliers. The highly technical products are designed for climbers, but the rapid brand growth has also been fueled by “gorpcore,” a fashion trend where technical gear is worn as high-end streetwear. 

WSJ got rare access inside Arc’teryx’s Canadian manufacturing facility ARC’One to learn how the company carved out a unique brand identity in an industry dominated by mainstream giants like Patagonia and The North Face.

videos.title: Inside Man: How Chinese Spies Used Lies, Romance And Betrayal To Target The Federal Reserve
videos.description:
One week after a friendly summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, CNBC details an aggressive plot by China to infiltrate one of the United States’ most important institutions: the Federal Reserve. This explosive documentary delves into the incredible saga of a Chinese spy's effort to obtain secrets from the inner confines of the U.S.' top bank. It's a tale of sex, money, deceit and betrayal that put some of the country’s vital economic and financial secrets at risk. With exclusive access to new documents, audio, photos and text messages, CNBC's Senior Washington Correspondent Eamon Javers uncovers the story of former Fed economist John Rogers and a Chinese spy posing as an economics student who he befriended in 2013. “Inside Man” is a spy story at the heart of the competition for global economic dominance, posing the question of whether Rogers was a spy himself or an unwitting dupe.

videos.title: Bangladesh's Rural Women and Youth Are Transforming Their Futures | RELI Project
videos.description:
What happens when women and young people gain access to skills, finance, and opportunities? Across 3,200 villages in Bangladesh, the Resilience, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Improvement (RELI) Project is helping vulnerable households build sustainable livelihoods, strengthen resilience, and create new economic opportunities. The project is helping to create jobs and opportunities for women, youth, and vulnerable communities through skills development, access to finance, market linkages, and community-driven initiatives. 

Watch this video to see how Hafiza and Rojina have become agri-entrepreneurs, gained economic independence, improved their families' well-being, and created jobs for local women.


ABOUT THE WORLD BANK 🌐 The World Bank is one of the world’s largest sources of funding and knowledge for low-income countries. Its five institutions share a commitment to reducing poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development on a livable planet. http://www.worldbank.org
